summary: The detail pass did its job on the parts. Inside corners are rounded or declared sharp with mostly valid reasons, the camera bosses went from a 22 % to a 73-84 % edge ring, the horn holes are teardrops, the FPC notch now goes through the plate, and every FEA, clearance and torque check passes with the hot spots where the load enters. It fails on one major: the generated ASSEMBLY.md step 6 (and its picture) has the tilt servo screwed into the yoke first and the bracket + horn pushed onto its spline afterwards. With 0.9 mm between the knuckle and the -Y wall and 3.2 mm of spline engagement, that cannot be done without springing the pivot wall about 2.5 mm, which would crack its root (the knock FEA puts 22 MPa there at only 1.3 mm). DESIGN.md section 8 has the right order, but the user-facing instructions now contradict it.

findings.issue: out/ASSEMBLY.md step 6 says: fit tilt_servo onto the yoke, drive its 2 x M2 x 6 tab screws, then 'join the step-2 sub-assembly: fit tilt_horn onto tilt_servo ... set the driven parts to 15 deg, then fit it'. step_06_iso.png draws the bracket coming in along -Y through the pivot wall. That cannot be done. The horn has to slide 3.2 mm (catalog spline_engage) toward +Y onto the spline, but the knuckle has only pivot_gap 0.9 mm to the -Y wall (layout: pin_wall_in = -(horn_y + pivot_gap)). DESIGN.md section 8 step 6 says so itself: 'the bracket has only 0.6 mm of axial room: it could not be slid onto a spline already in place'. Following the generated instructions means spreading the 5 mm pivot wall about 2.5 mm. yoke_knock_in shows 1.26 mm already gives a 22 MPa peak at the wall root, so roughly 2.5 mm would reach about 44 MPa, above PETG's 39 MPa across layers: the yoke cracks. This regressed when the 15-degree horn-centring text was added, because the engine now joins the horn sub-assembly after its parent servo. The ASSEMBLY.md step also never says where the tilt-horn centre screw is driven from (through the -Y wall's pivot hole and the 2.4 mm knuckle hole, before the shoulder screw). Nothing in kerf checks the tilt servo's insertion path: only pan_servo has an `insert:` entry.
findings.fix: In project.yaml, give tilt_servo `insert: {direction: [0, -1, 0], distance: 30}` (it goes in from outside the +Y wall, moving -Y) so kerf checks that path. Also give it an assembly_note: 'FIRST hold the bracket + tilt horn between the yoke walls at +15 deg (camera tipped up, mid-travel), horn toward the +Y wall; then push the servo in from outside, case top through the window, spline into the horn hub; 2 x M2 x 6 through the tabs; then drive the horn centre screw through the -Y wall pivot hole and the 2.4 mm knuckle hole; only then the shoulder screw.' Better still, make the engine general: when a child sub-assembly's joint is axially trapped (spline engage > the free axial gap, or project.yaml says so), the generated step places the sub-assembly first and inserts the parent servo into it. The text and the picture should then follow that order. Add a test for it. Add the +15 deg hold to DESIGN.md section 8 step 6.

findings.issue: The camera-rear trim box starts 0.01 mm in front of the plate face (bracket.py: `Pos(0, 0, -p.standoff + 0.01)`). It removes the inner 1.4 mm of each r 3.6 boss but leaves a 0.01 mm skin of the boss footprint on the plate face. That skin, and the steps it makes, are the stray vertical lines and C-shaped steps on each boss in part_bracket_right/iso. A slicer ignores it, but it is degenerate geometry that the edge, fillet and FEA meshing tools then have to handle.
findings.fix: Subtract the keep-out zone from each standoff before `body += so` (so the trim never touches the plate), or start the trim box exactly at the plate face (xf).

findings.issue: Outside edges are not broken on the bracket or most of the yoke. ENGINEERING.md s5 asks for a 0.5-1 mm chamfer or fillet, and project.yaml declares `style: edge_break: 0.5`, but only the base applies it (r 4 plan corners, 0.6/0.8 chamfers). The bracket has a 0.4 mm bed chamfer and nothing else: the camera-plate and arm top edges, the front vertical edges and the boss rims are knife-sharp. On the yoke, the plate top edges, the wall vertical edges, the pivot-wall sides and the gusset edges are sharp. The product's edge language is not consistent.
findings.fix: After the booleans, chamfer or fillet the remaining convex edges at 0.5 mm (a features helper that breaks every convex edge except mating faces would serve every project). Raise the bracket bed chamfer to 0.5.

findings.issue: The 'servo cavity: the SG90's square case and tabs slide along it' reason is right for the deck-underside corners over the tabs and the tab-level walls. It is wrong for the cavity FLOOR corners (sharp_kept at [0, 6.6, 9.0] len 33.2 and [+-16.6, -3.2, 9.0] len 19.7). The servo sits CAV_DROP = 1 mm above that floor and 0.5 mm off the walls, so an r 1 cove there never touches it. These corners are cold (96 % of the base is cold), so this is about craft, not strength.
findings.fix: Narrow the `mating` keep in base.py to z >= cav_z + 0.5 so the floor corners get the style r 1 (or r 0.5).

findings.issue: DESIGN.md section 4 calls the deck legs over the cavity 'short bridges'. They are not bridges. They are 4.7 mm ledges (cav_x 33.2 vs window 23.8) anchored on the end wall and the back wall (two adjacent sides) with free edges on the window and open -Y sides, so they are cantilever overhangs. Their underside is exactly the seat for the pan servo's tab tops, and the M2 pilots start there. In PETG they will droop at the free corners, so the servo can sit tilted.
findings.fix: Paint supports (or a tree support) under the two deck ledges inside the cavity in the plate 3MF and the base print note ('supports: allowed' is already set), or check the droop in the slicer preview when you print the base first. Correct the wording in DESIGN.md section 4.

findings.issue: Carried forward and still open: ASSEMBLY.md never mentions the 1/4-20 nut (step 1 just says 'Start with base'). The nut drops in through the open -Y side across the cavity floor. Once the pan servo is in, the gap between the cavity floor and the servo bottom is only 1 mm, so a user who follows ASSEMBLY.md has to unscrew the servo to fit the nut. The 8 mm maximum tripod-screw protrusion (A2) is also only in DESIGN.md.
findings.fix: Add an assembly_note on pan_servo (or on base): 'drop the 1/4-20 nut into its floor pocket (flats across Y) BEFORE the servo; tripod screw protrusion 5.5-8 mm max'.

findings.issue: Tilt-horn centre screw: the BOM says 'M2 horn centre screw, comes with the servo ... a drop of medium threadlocker: metal into metal'. The SG90's output gear is plastic (nylon). The stock screw is a Phillips self-tapper going into plastic, not metal into metal, and anaerobic threadlocker can stress-crack plastics. DESIGN.md section 8 step 7 says the screw is driven 'with a 1.5 mm key' through the 4 mm pivot hole and the 2.4 mm knuckle hole. A 1.5 mm key does not drive the stock Phillips screw, and a PH00 driver needs a shaft of 2.4 mm or less and about 40 mm of reach.
findings.fix: Either buy an M2 socket-head centre screw (length from the horn hub plus spline depth) and list it in bom_extra, or state 'PH00 driver, 2 mm shaft, 40 mm or more' in the note. Drop the threadlocker advice for plastic-gear servos: the engine note should follow the servo's gear material.

findings.issue: Carried forward: the knock cases pass on p99.9 (9.71 / 9.15 of 13 MPa), but the volume peaks are 22.2 / 18.2 MPa and the surface peak is 14.4 MPa (hot zone [3.3, -11.2, 6.1] at 1.11 x the allowable). The peaks sit at the fixed pan-horn screw holes and the pivot-wall root, so they are partly support singularities. The case is also conservative, since all 30 N goes into one wall where the real bracket shares it with both. Elastic travel of 1.3-1.6 mm is accepted by the relaxed 2.0 mm limit. The +Y servo window edge looks ragged where the 14 mm gear-boss relief bites about 0.7 mm into each side of the 12.6 mm window.
findings.fix: Optionally go to r 2.5 at the pivot-wall root or put a gusset on the inside of the pivot wall below the bracket swing. Optionally make the gear-boss relief clear of the window sides (a counterbore that stops short of the window), so the window edges stay straight.

findings.issue: Carried forward: base_fea fixes the whole bottom face (engine warning: no fastener site is held). On the uplift side of the knock, the bonded face carries tension that the real joint gets only from the 1/4-20 screw. The hot spot is still in the right place (deck pilots, 9.17 MPa peak, 6.16 p99.9). The pan tab screws' pull-out under the knock moment (about 45 N on the far M2 in 3.6 mm of PETG) is still not computed.
findings.fix: Optionally add a support case that fixes the compression side plus the nut-floor ring, and pull-test the tab screws on the first base print (DESIGN.md section 10 already says to print the base first).

findings.issue: DESIGN.md has stale numbers after this pass. Section 5 says the camera standoffs are 'r 2.8' (now r 3.6). The section 7 table gives yoke_fea peak 4.0 (now 4.81) and knock 9.55 / 9.31 p99.9 with peaks 17.8 / 22.0 (now 9.15 / 9.71 with 18.19 / 22.20). Sections 4 and 10 give bracket overhang 3.5 % / 1.2 % (now 0.44 %). The section 3 masses (yoke 16.0, bracket 7.6) are now 15.9 / 7.8. Also carried forward: horn, bolt circle and SG90 tab dimensions are catalog estimates; measure them before printing the bracket and yoke.
